title: Minimal reproduction and regression
goal: Reduce a failure to one distinguishing input and keep the check reproducible after the repair.

prerequisites.text: Checking the remainder after strtol, boundary cases and recording run results separately from build errors.

terms.title: Minimal reproduction
terms.definition: A small source and input that reproduce the same fault without unrelated conditions.

terms.title: Regression case
terms.definition: A saved check where the same input distinguishes the faulty version from the fixed version.

terms.title: Run record
terms.definition: The source or its revision, environment, exact input, output, stderr and exit status.

sections.title: Keep the input that separates the versions
paragraphs: The contract permits surrounding whitespace, with no other characters after the number. If the old version prints 7 for 7x, reduce the full example to that one line. The line 7 succeeds in both versions.
Before changing the code, record the expected invalid and the observed 7. After the change, use the same input file. The check can catch the same fault if it returns.

sections.title: Compare 7x with a number surrounded by spaces
paragraphs: For 7x, strtol returns 7 and leaves end pointing to x. For the line with trailing spaces, end reaches the end after skipping them. The *end != '\0' check makes the distinction explicit.
steps: Supply 7x. Parsing finds the prefix 7. The suffix check rejects x and the program prints invalid.
Run with the line “ 7 ”. The allowed whitespace is skipped. Stdout is 7 followed by a newline.
Both cases finish with status 0 and empty stderr. The contract defines invalid as a normal response to rejected input.

sections.title: Record the phase that stopped
paragraphs: The separate _Static_assert rejection is an expected build outcome. There is no program stdout for that build. A launch environment failure is also separate from invalid printed by a running program.

Log the source, compiler version, C17 mode, exact input, expected and observed stdout, stderr and exit status. Keep inputs and expected program output independent of random values, compiler message localisation and time.

Make the log reproducible. Use a short input, and write down its exact spaces and LF. Use the same compiler version and the identical line before and after the fix. Keep at least one normal case alongside it to ensure the fix did not turn every answer into invalid.

sections.title: Capture a booking regression
paragraphs: The practice accepts a seat count from 0 through 30 and prints slots with the number. Pin 12x, which incorrectly gives slots 12 in the starter. After the repair, repeat it and a valid input with surrounding spaces. Record the exact output lines so the comparison is reproducible.
When sharing the run record, identify the source version or include a copy. Describe a line ending as LF or explicitly note that it was absent.

reading.author: ISO/IEC JTC1/SC22/WG14
reading.title: ISO/IEC 9899:2018 — Programming languages — C
reading.purpose: Reduce a failure to one distinguishing input and keep the check reproducible after the repair.

selfcheck.prompt: Which input distinguishes the fixed version from the prefix-accepting version?
feedback: Both versions accept a plain number.

selfcheck.prompt: The build rejected _Static_assert. What should you record?
options: A build rejection, with no program run
feedback: An executable that never ran has no observed exit status.

selfcheck.prompt: What does another person need to reproduce the difference on 12x?
selfcheck.feedback: The exact source or revision, compiler version and C17 mode, the single 12x input with its newline, expected stdout, stderr and exit status, and separate observations for the old and fixed versions.

practice.title: A seat-count regression check
practice.task: Parse the first line as an integer from 0 to 30. Allow an optional sign and surrounding whitespace, and reject any other suffix. Print slots and the number with a separating space, or invalid. Record what the starter does with 12x, fix the suffix check, and keep the same input and control cases in your log.

cases.label: Second number on the same line

criteria: 12x gives invalid, and 12 surrounded by spaces gives slots 12.
0 and 30 are accepted, while 31 gives invalid. A normal result has empty stderr and status 0.
Keep the source or revision, the input with its exact line ending and separate before-and-after observations.
practice.hint: Keep the input where the versions disagree. Compare where number parsing stopped with where a valid complete line should end. Run a nearby valid input separately.

steps.action: Record the expected invalid and run the starter with 12x.
steps.why: This short input distinguishes the two versions.
steps.expected: The starter prints slots 12 with empty stderr and status 0.

steps.action: Fix the branch where *end points to a non-whitespace character. Rerun 12x and then 12 with surrounding spaces.
steps.why: Confirm suffix rejection and that valid whitespace still works.
steps.expected: The separate results are invalid and slots 12.

steps.action: Add 30 and 31 to the log with exact expectations and rerun the tests.
steps.why: The parser fix should preserve the upper-bound rule.

exercises.title: Independent transfer
exercises.task: In a separate copy, use 0–9 and save one minimal input with a suffix, a valid boundary and its outer neighbour.
criteria: For example, 9x gives invalid, 9 gives slots 9 and 10 gives invalid. The log records exact stdin bytes, stdout and status for every run.

teaching.scene: An operator found that a number with an extra letter can sometimes be accepted. Make a short record another person can use to reproduce the failure and verify the fix.

predict.prompt: The example receives 7x followed by LF. What part does strtol convert? What stops the remaining processing, and what will stdout contain?
predict.answer: strtol consumes 7 and leaves end at x. The x is neither whitespace nor the end of the string. read_value rejects the input, and main prints invalid.

apply.prompt: Make a pair with the number 12 and a plus sign: put the sign before the number on one line and after it on the other. Add LF to both. Which new input catches a version that checks only the numeric prefix?
apply.answer: +12 parses through the end of the line, so the output is 12. After 12+, end is left at the plus sign, so the answer should be invalid. A version that accepts a numeric prefix would incorrectly also print 12 for the second line.

practice.strategy: Preserve the exact input 12x followed by LF and record stdout, stderr, and exit status. After the fix, use the same bytes and add a valid control with 12 and permitted whitespace.
practice.diagnosis: If both cases are rejected after the change, check whether the parser still permits trailing whitespace. If it accepts 12 3, inspect the end-of-string check after skipping whitespace.

syntax.form:
long value = strtol(line, &end, 10);
/* Check whether a number was consumed and inspect its suffix. */
syntax.explanation: strtol consumes the numeric prefix and reports where it stopped. The check after skipping whitespace enforces the contract for the rest of the line.
syntax.mistake: A successful example alone does not reproduce the original defect. Keep the original failing input alongside a control that must remain accepted.
